metadata.title: SPARC Security Scanning and System Integrity

components.title: SPARC Application
components.description: SPARC (Systematic Policy and Regulatory Compliance) is a Rails application for managing NIST 800-53 compliance documentation. This component definition covers vulnerability scanning, flaw remediation, and system integrity controls.

implemented-requirements.description: The scanner output SPARC hands onward is attributable to the instance that produced it. The HDF package — amendments (only when they pass hdf amend verify, #1325), findings and disposition summaries — is HMAC-SHA256 signed with an instance key derived from SPARC_HASH via SparcKeyDerivation, so a consumer can prove the package came from this SPARC instance and was not altered. Each disposition carries a signature_hash binding both the person who decided it and the person who approved it, so a risk acceptance cannot be repudiated by either.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/hdf_package_service.rb, app/lib/sparc_key_derivation.rb and app/models/finding_disposition.rb (#809, #862).

implemented-requirements.description: Re-occurrence is never silent. Every ingest writes a per-scan-run ScannerFinding row and demotes the prior row to superseded rather than overwriting it, so the full scan history — and each finding's computed lifecycle state (new, carried_forward, re_failed, expired) — remains reconstructable as an audit record. Disposition approve/reject decisions and aggregation runs emit AuditEvent rows through the API base controller's audit_log helper.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/hdf_ingest_service.rb#record_finding, app/models/scanner_finding.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/finding_dispositions_controller.rb and app/controllers/api/v1/aggregations_controller.rb (#811, #862).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC performs automated vulnerability scanning through multiple tools in the CI security workflow: Trivy filesystem and container image scanning for CVEs in dependencies and base images, CodeQL semantic analysis for code-level vulnerabilities, bundler-audit for Ruby gem advisory checks, and Grype SBOM-driven SCA (#461) that consumes the CycloneDX SBOMs produced by sbom_generation and the Trivy fs/container scans. Grype provides authoritative vulnerability matching against the published SBOM artifacts that downstream consumers receive — the SBOM is scan-verified, not just generated. Scan results are uploaded as SARIF to GitHub Security for centralized tracking; Grype JSON is normalized to HDF via SAF CLI (anchoregrype2hdf). All container image CVE findings are triaged and dispositioned in docs/compliance/sparc-findings.yml with severity classification, deployment-specific rationale, NIST control mapping, and 30-day review cycles. Tenant-supplied scan results are attributable to what they assessed (#811): an ingested HDF scan records the target CdefDocument it ran against and a scanner_scope of 'target' (component-specific scanners such as Trivy or Gitleaks) or 'boundary' (system-wide posture scanners), and each resulting ScannerFinding carries component_ref and source_location. Vulnerability results therefore roll up per component, not only per authorization boundary. Findings are retained per scan run rather than overwritten, so scan-over-scan history is preserved for the authorization boundary. A disposition for a static-analysis RULE covers only the results it was reviewed against (#1186): register entries for a CodeQL rule pin each result by path and CodeQL line fingerprint, and the security gate fails when the live results differ in either direction, so a new instance of a dispositioned rule is never waived unreviewed. On the Red Hat UBI 10 base (#1200), Trivy reports no vulnerabilities for RHEL 10.2 while Grype reads Red Hat's el10 advisory data, so the Grype container scan is gated at HIGH alongside Trivy and register dispositions reach it under Grype's requirement names. Each detected vulnerability carries the provider's FedRAMP evaluation (#1354, FedRAMP VER-EVA): internet-reachable, likely exploitable, the Potential Agency Impact N-rating (N0-N5) with its history, when it was evaluated and the planned next reduction. It is keyed by boundary and control so it survives every rescan.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (Trivy, CodeQL, bundler-audit, grype_sbom_scan). Results uploaded to GitHub Security tab. Container vulnerability baseline: docs/compliance/sparc-findings.yml (76 CVEs triaged, 4 HIGH accepted with mitigating controls, 1 MEDIUM remediated). Grype --fail-on starts at 'critical' for ramp; bumped to 'high' once baseline is triaged. Org SCA pipeline (#616): .github/workflows/sbom-and-sca.yml additionally runs the org-shared reusable Grype + Trivy fs scan (gate=CRITICAL, allow-list .security/sca-allowlist.yaml) on every main push and a daily cron, re-scanning unchanged dependencies against fresh CVE feeds. #811: HdfIngestService records cdef_document_id + scanner_scope on ScanRun and component_ref/source_location on ScannerFinding; app/models/scan_run.rb, app/models/scanner_finding.rb. bin/codeql_pin_check.rb and the pinned_results field of docs/compliance/sparc-findings.yml, enforced by bin/sparc_findings_to_hdf_amendments.rb. FedRAMP evaluation: app/models/fedramp_vulnerability_evaluation.rb, app/services/fedramp_evaluation_service.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/fedramp_evaluations_controller.rb (#1354).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC supply chain controls: CycloneDX SBOM generation for Ruby gems (cyclonedx-ruby) and container/filesystem (Trivy); known-good version pinning in Gemfile.lock; container image digest pinning. SBOM-driven vulnerability scanning via Grype (#461) means the supply-chain artifacts downstream consumers actually receive are vulnerability-tested before release, closing the gap where SBOMs were generated as evidence but never scanned themselves. External framework content (#1115, #1172): FedRAMP's consolidated rules are vendored byte-for-byte with a provenance record pinning the upstream commit and the sha256 of each file, verified by the test suite; the application never fetches them at run time, and bin/ksi_upstream_diff.rb reports upstream change for review before any re-vendor.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (sbom_generation, trivy_fs_scan, trivy_container_scan, grype_sbom_scan). SBOMs and Grype findings published to the sparc-compliance-latest artifact consumed by sparc-iac. Org-wide SCA rollup (#616, umbrella container-build-sign#12): .github/workflows/sbom-and-sca.yml emits the source CycloneDX to s3://<security-artifacts-bucket>/<EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY>/{<YYYY-MM-DD>,latest}/sparc/sca/sparc.cdx.json via GitHub OIDC for central OWASP Dependency-Track aggregation (hub-and-spoke). The s3:PutObject role (SPARC_APP_CI_ARN) is provisioned cross-repo in sparc-iac; the emit step degrades to artifact-only until it exists. The app image SBOM is separately cosign-attested (--type cyclonedx) in build-sign-publish.yml. lib/data/fedramp/ (vendored rules, schema, provenance sidecar), spec/lib/data/fedramp_vendored_rules_spec.rb, bin/ksi_upstream_diff.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC verifies component authenticity through Gemfile.lock specific-version pins, container image provenance, and CycloneDX SBOM tracking of component origins. Grype SBOM scanning (#461) augments this by matching each SBOM-declared component against Anchore's vulnerability database — components whose declared identity in the SBOM matches known-vulnerable versions are surfaced as CI failures. The release also publishes an OpenVEX attestation of the vulnerability posture (#917), signed with cosign and bound to the image digest. Each statement names the image it describes by purl and digest rather than a converter placeholder (#1144), and the release asserts that identity against the digest being attested, so the document remains interpretable when read apart from its in-toto subject. Every file the image build downloads is verified against a pinned value before it is used (#1380): the Ruby and jemalloc source tarballs by SHA-256, the AWS RDS CA bundle by ADD --checksum, the golang build image and the Dockerfile frontend by digest, the hdf-libs source by the commit its release tag must resolve to, and each of NIST's OSCAL JSON and XSD schemas by the SHA-256 in lib/oscal_schema_pins.json. Each value is checked against two publisher sources where they exist, and a changed or substituted download fails the build.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in Gemfile.lock and .github/workflows/security.yml (grype_sbom_scan); build-time download verification in Dockerfile (#1380).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC's runtime CDEF ingestion (#466) treats external authoritative sources as a tracked supply chain. The AWS Labs OSCAL Component Definitions repository (awslabs/oscal-content-for-aws-services) is enumerated via the GitHub Trees API, fetched per-blob with the blob SHA recorded for integrity, and imported only after OSCAL spec-version filtering against SPARC's loaded schemas. Each imported row carries source_url, source_sha, source_commit_sha, and fetched_at provenance fields. The feature is opt-in via SPARC_AWS_LABS_CDEF_ENABLED so air-gapped deployments are unaffected; an ETag-conditional fetch makes the daily refresh near-zero cost when nothing has changed upstream.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/aws_labs_cdef_import_service.rb + aws_labs_cdef_source_client.rb. License compliance (Apache 2.0 inheritance from upstream): NOTICE + LICENSES/AWS-LABS-OSCAL-CONTENT-LICENSE + docs/compliance/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Read-only + clone-to-amend policy preserves upstream content untouched while letting tenants tailor derivatives.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC addresses flaw remediation through automated vulnerability detection and dependency update tooling. Trivy identifies CVEs in container images and filesystem dependencies. Bundler-audit checks Ruby gems against the Ruby Advisory Database. Dependabot automatically creates pull requests for vulnerable or outdated dependencies. Accepted container findings are documented in docs/compliance/sparc-findings.yml with deployment-agnostic mitigating controls (non-root container, reverse proxy, TLS, network whitelisting, seccomp isolation) and 30-day review cycles for re-evaluation. Remediation timelines for tenant scanner findings are enforced by data rather than convention (#809). A disposition (HDF Amendment) suppresses its finding only when it has been approved — by an Instance Admin or a role holding the amendment.approve permission — and only while inside its validity window. AmendmentValidityService resolves that window from the boundary profile's ODP value, falling back to the admin-provisioned RemediationTimeline SLA grid (baseline level Low/Moderate/High x NIST criticality Critical/High/Moderate/Low/Informational/Unknown to days), measured from the control's first-discovered scan; an open POA&M addressing the control confers validity for as long as it stays open. When the window lapses the finding returns to the triage board as 'expired' and routes to re-approval instead of continuing to suppress. A finding that was passing or already dispositioned and then fails again, or fails at a worse severity, is classified 're_failed' and surfaced as a regression distinct from steady-state known risk.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml and .github/dependabot.yml. Automated PR creation for vulnerable dependencies. Container baseline: docs/compliance/sparc-findings.yml tracks remediation status per CVE. #809: app/services/amendment_validity_service.rb, app/models/remediation_timeline.rb, app/controllers/admin/remediation_timelines_controller.rb (admin SLA grid, seeded defaults). Lifecycle computed in app/services/hdf_ingest_service.rb#lifecycle_for. The seeded SLA values are a starting point and are expected to be replaced by the organization's own remediation policy.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC implements malicious code protection through Gitleaks secret scanning to detect accidentally committed credentials and secrets, and Trivy container scanning to identify known malware signatures and vulnerable packages in the deployment image. Both tools run automatically in the CI pipeline on every code change. Gitleaks CI scanning includes custom regex rules in .gitleaks.toml that detect leaked SPARC API tokens (sparc_ prefix) and service account tokens (sparc_sa_ prefix), preventing application-specific secrets from reaching the repository.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (Gitleaks, Trivy container scan). Custom Gitleaks rules defined in .gitleaks.toml (sparc-api-token and sparc-service-account-token patterns).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC supports system monitoring through structured logging to STDOUT in the production environment, enabling integration with external log aggregation services such as AWS CloudWatch. Audit events provide application-level monitoring of security-relevant actions. The production configuration is optimized for centralized log collection and analysis.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in config/environments/production.rb and app/models/audit_event.rb. Logs are CloudWatch-ready.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC receives security alerts through multiple channels: Dependabot alerts for vulnerable Ruby gems and container base image updates, GitHub Security tab aggregation of SARIF-formatted scan results from Trivy and CodeQL, and bundler-audit advisories. These alerts provide timely notification of security-relevant changes affecting the application.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (SARIF uploads) and .github/dependabot.yml.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC verifies software integrity through CycloneDX SBOM generation that inventories all software components and their versions. Docker image builds produce digest-verified images, and the CI pipeline ensures that only tested and scanned artifacts are promoted to deployment. The SBOM provides a verifiable record of the software supply chain. SPARC also verifies the integrity of its own database schema before it serves (#1151): the container entrypoint reconciles the schema against db/schema.rb additively and then verifies it, and refuses to start the web server on structural drift; the unauthenticated /up/ready readiness probe reports schema drift to the load balancer (counts only), so an instance whose schema stops matching is taken out of service. Findings dispositions are tamper-evident: the HDF amendment chain must be established, not merely unbroken, or the security gate fails (#1184). The image build verifies the integrity of every source and toolchain it downloads against pinned SHA-256 values, digests and commits, and fails on a mismatch (#1380). The schemas SPARC validates exchanged documents against are vendored byte for byte and pinned by SHA-256: FedRAMP's package schemas (lib/data/fedramp/fedramp-schemas.provenance.json) and the XCCDF 1.2 schema set (lib/data/xccdf/xccdf.provenance.json). A file that is not the pinned one stops SPARC from using any of them (#1354).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (CycloneDX SBOM, Docker image digests). Schema integrity: bin/docker-entrypoint, app/services/schema_drift_service.rb, app/services/schema_reconciliation_service.rb, app/controllers/health_controller.rb. Chain gate: bin/hdf_amend_chain_gate.rb in .github/workflows/security.yml (security_gate). Build-time download integrity: Dockerfile (#1380). Pinned exchange schemas: app/services/fedramp_package_schemas.rb and app/services/xccdf_schema.rb (#1354). Scan provenance (#1354): ScanRun.raw_hdf_digest is the SHA-256 of the HDF bytes as uploaded and the stored file is that upload, also when a v2 document is converted to v3 for reading (app/services/hdf_ingest_service.rb).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC validates information inputs through multiple layers: Brakeman SAST scanning detects injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the codebase, Rails strong parameters enforce allowlisting of permitted request parameters in all controllers, and ActiveRecord validations enforce data type and format constraints at the model level. Avatar upload validates content type against an allowlist (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP) and enforces a 2 MB file size limit at both client-side (Stimulus controller) and server-side (ProfilesController strong params and User model ActiveStorage validations). Client-side Cropper.js constrains canvas output to 256x256 pixels before upload. Evidence artifact upload via the REST API (POST /api/v1/evidences) accepts arbitrary artifact content by design (PDF, images, logs, scan output), so it is defended by an executable-signature deny-list rather than a MIME allowlist: the first 32 bytes are checked against known executable magic bytes (PE/MS-DOS, ELF, Mach-O, Java class, WebAssembly, and shebang scripts) and the upload is rejected with HTTP 422 before persistence. The upload size cap is enforced model-side by the AttachmentSizeLimit concern. Temporal input validation (#903): Evidence#collected_at is rejected when it is in the future, because a collection timestamp later than now is impossible on its face and, if persisted, would place incorrect provenance metadata into an exported OSCAL evidence package. The web and API create paths both server-stamp the value and never permit it as a request parameter, so the model validation is the backstop for any path that later can set it (console, data migration, admin tooling, a newly permitted parameter). The validation is scoped to changed values so an existing record holding a bad timestamp remains correctable. Documents exchanged with other systems are checked before SPARC accepts them (#1354): DocumentValidationService validates FedRAMP package JSON, OSCAL, HDF and XCCDF against SPARC's pinned schemas, and SchemaCompleteness rejects a required field that is present but blank, which FedRAMP's schemas alone accept.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in .github/workflows/security.yml (Brakeman), all controllers (strong params), and models (validations). Avatar input validation in app/controllers/profiles_controller.rb, app/models/user.rb, and app/javascript/controllers/avatar_crop_controller.js. Evidence upload validation in app/controllers/api/v1/evidences_controller.rb (reject_if_executable_signature!), reusing the FileUploadable::EXECUTABLE_MAGIC_BYTES table, with the size cap in app/models/concerns/attachment_size_limit.rb. Tested by spec/ (incl. the executable-rejection case in spec/requests/api/v1/evidences_spec.rb), tests/api/test_evidences.py, and Brakeman scan. Temporal validation in app/models/evidence.rb (collected_at_not_in_future), covered by spec/models/evidence_spec.rb and the future-value rejection cases in spec/requests/evidences_spec.rb and spec/requests/api/v1/evidences_spec.rb (#903). Exchanged-document validation in app/services/document_validation_service.rb, app/services/schema_completeness.rb and app/controllers/api/v1/document_validations_controller.rb (#1354). HDF ingest (#1354): app/services/hdf_ingest_service.rb validates every uploaded HDF document with the pinned hdf CLI (hdf validate --type results, --schema-ver 2 for HDF v2) after the size cap and strict JSON parse, converts v2 up with hdf convert --from hdf@2 --to hdf@3, and refuses with a 422 before persisting anything; app/services/hdf_runner.rb runs each call with a fixed argv, no shell, a timeout and a size-checked output. Tested by spec/services/hdf_ingest_service_spec.rb and spec/services/hdf_runner_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC treats approving an amendment as a distinct authorization act from triaging one. Setting a disposition requires evidence.write; approving or rejecting it requires admin or the amendment.approve permission key, seeded to the AO, Agency AO and ISSM roles — the roles that accept residual risk. Every triage endpoint remains boundary-scoped, so the permission is evaluated against the boundary whose risk is being accepted. Every download of a boundary's triage data (dispositions as HDF amendments, the signed package, and the OSCAL POA&M) requires evidence.read on that boundary. The POA&M download ran no check from v1.17.9 to v1.17.10, fixed in v1.17.11 (#1354).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/role.rb (PERMISSION_KEYS), app/controllers/api/v1/finding_dispositions_controller.rb#authorize_approve! and db/seeds.rb. Tested by spec/models/role_spec.rb and spec/requests/api/v1/finding_dispositions_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces separation of duties within the finding disposition workflow. The person who decides a disposition (decided_by) and the person who approves it (approved_by) are recorded independently, and a draft disposition has no suppressing effect on a finding until an approver acts. One account cannot both accept a scanner risk and authorise its acceptance in a single step.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/finding_disposition.rb and app/controllers/api/v1/finding_dispositions_controller.rb. Tested by spec/models/finding_disposition_spec.rb and spec/requests/api/v1/finding_dispositions_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: Undispositioned scanner risk becomes a tracked POA&M item automatically rather than by re-keying. A failed finding that is not suppressed by an applicable, approved, in-window falsePositive, waiver or inherited disposition is upserted as a PoamFinding on the boundary's POA&M, keyed as HDF: <control-id>. The operation is idempotent, so re-aggregation updates the existing item instead of duplicating it.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/hdf_aggregation_service.rb#aggregate_poam and app/models/poam_finding.rb. Tested by spec/services/hdf_aggregation_service_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: Continuous monitoring output reaches the authorization package instead of stopping at a worklist. HdfAggregationService maps each current finding to the NIST control or controls named in its HDF tags.nist and writes a dedicated hdf_scan_result annotation field on the matching SSP, SAP and SAR controls. The write is non-destructive: authored narrative is never overwritten. It runs on demand or asynchronously through AggregateFindingsJob. Continuous monitoring of the running system includes the /up (liveness) and /up/ready (readiness: database, pending migrations, schema drift) probes (#1151), and a CI job that upgrades a database built by the last published release with each change and fails on schema drift. A boundary's FedRAMP Vulnerability Detail Report and Accepted Vulnerability Info (FedRAMP VER-RPT-VDT, VER-RPT-AVI; effective 2026-12-07) are built from its findings, dispositions and FedRAMP evaluations for a report period. A vulnerability not remediated within 192 days of evaluation is reported as accepted (VER-TFR-MAV). The boundary's Historical Vulnerability Activity (VER-TFR-MRH) carries both lists in one snapshot for automated retrieval, by default for the 12 months ending now (#1390). Each report is validated against FedRAMP's pinned schema and for completeness before it is returned (#1354).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/hdf_aggregation_service.rb, app/jobs/aggregate_findings_job.rb and app/controllers/api/v1/aggregations_controller.rb. Tested by spec/services/hdf_aggregation_service_spec.rb. app/controllers/health_controller.rb; bin/upgrade_path_check and the upgrade_path job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (advisory until promoted). FedRAMP reports: app/services/fedramp_vulnerability_report_service.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/fedramp_reports_controller.rb (#1354).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC distinguishes regression from steady-state known risk across scans. A finding that was passing or dispositioned and then fails again — or fails at a worse severity than before — is classified re_failed and surfaced distinctly on the triage board, so a control that has regressed is not lost among findings that were already known and accepted.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/hdf_ingest_service.rb#lifecycle_for and app/controllers/hdf_triage_controller.rb. Tested by spec/services/hdf_ingest_service_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: An amendment is a time-bounded risk decision, not a permanent suppression. AmendmentValidityService computes valid_until from the boundary profile's baseline level and the finding's NIST criticality, measured from the scan that first discovered the control rather than from the date the amendment was written. An open POA&M addressing the control confers validity for as long as it stays open. When an amendment expires it stops suppressing, and the finding returns to the triage board as expired for re-approval.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/amendment_validity_service.rb and app/models/remediation_timeline.rb. Tested by spec/services/amendment_validity_service_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC exchanges FedRAMP, OSCAL, HDF and XCCDF documents with other systems only through registered connections (#1354). An administrator, or a holder of connections.manage, registers each one: the provider's FedRAMP ID and certification class, the root trust-center address, each document to pull, and the boundary its documents land in. Every document received, pulled or uploaded, is validated against SPARC's pinned schema and for completeness, stored once by SHA-256 and never overwritten, and takes effect for its boundary only when a reviewer of the receiving boundary accepts it. The uploader cannot decide their own upload. Only a byte-identical re-delivery skips review. SPARC serves its own documents back out through an exchange index, and records who read it. A provider may also push a changed document, signed with an Ed25519 key pinned on the connection (at most two, for rotation): SPARC accepts it only within 5 minutes of its timestamp, once per signature, from inside the connection's IP ranges and within the upload limit, then pulls the document fresh from its registered address. Matching bytes confirm the push; anything else is received as an unconfirmed push, flagged and never auto-accepted. A Class A connection records the alternative security framework its certification rests on (FedRAMP FRC-CLA-ASF) and its date, flags it expired 12 months later, and receives the assessment materials behind it (FRC-CLA-EAM) as reviewed documents of the boundary, kept by SHA-256 and never served back out. SPARC also writes the boundary's FedRAMP Certification Package Overview (FRC-CSO-PKG) from the boundary's FedRAMP fields and contacts, validated against FedRAMP's pinned schema and for completeness before it is served; the overview address FedRAMP's reports name is the provider's trust center or, by the boundary's choice, SPARC's own authenticated overview endpoint (#1390). FedRAMP is turned on per boundary, with its certification profile (type, path, class); the boundary records its answer to each FedRAMP rule that applies to that profile, read from the vendored FedRAMP Consolidated Rules, and to each Key Security Indicator, each change audited and counted as a new Security Decision Record version (#1390). SPARC writes the boundary's Security Decision Record (SDR-CSO-FRR) from those answers and from its SSP's controls, parameters, ports and protocols, validated against FedRAMP's pinned schema before it is served, and lists what FedRAMP still requires of it (#1390). A boundary also records every change it evaluated, routine changes included, as the auditable record FedRAMP requires (SCN-CSO-MAR); SPARC computes each Significant Change Notification's deadline in federal business days (weekends and US federal holidays excluded) and writes the notification, validated before it is served, keeping each notice exactly as sent and listing 12 months of them in the exchange index. Its FedRAMP incidents, readable and writable only with their own permissions (incident.read, incident.write), carry their N-rating history and the Initial, Ongoing and Final Incident Report deadlines FedRAMP sets by class and N-rating; SPARC writes each report, validated before it is served, keeps each report exactly as sent, and never lists incidents in the exchange index (#1390). SPARC writes the boundary's quarterly Ongoing Certification Report (CCM-OCR-AVL) from its FedRAMP answers, significant changes, accepted vulnerabilities, reportable incidents and the agencies using the service, validated before it is served; reading it needs incident.read as well as evidence.read, and each report issued is kept exactly as issued, with its SHA-256 (#1390).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/exchange_connection.rb, app/models/received_document.rb, app/services/received_document_service.rb, app/services/received_document_review_service.rb, app/services/exchange_pull_service.rb, app/services/exchange_index_service.rb, app/services/exchange_push_service.rb, app/services/exchange_push_confirm_service.rb, app/services/certification_material_service.rb and the Api::V1 exchange controllers (#1354); tested by spec/services/exchange_push_service_spec.rb and spec/requests/api/v1/exchange_pushes_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC reaches an external provider's trust center only under that connection's pins (#1354). ExchangeFetcher allows only the hosts of the connection's registered addresses, and resolves DNS once. It refuses private, loopback, link-local (including cloud metadata), carrier-grade NAT and other non-public addresses unless the connection's own IP ranges include them, then connects to the vetted address. It checks the TLS certificate and, when pinned, the public key's SHA-256 (two pins allow rotation). It follows no redirects and caps size and time. The credential SPARC presents is encrypted at rest and never shown again. A push from the provider never chooses what SPARC fetches: the confirming pull reads only the document's registered address, under the same pins.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/services/exchange_fetcher.rb and app/models/exchange_connection.rb; tested by spec/services/exchange_fetcher_spec.rb, including a real TLS socket (#1354).
